question: What does this sign indicate?
choices: A school area — reduced speed limits apply when children are present
A playground ahead
A pedestrian crosswalk ahead
A daycare drop-off zone
explanation: The school zone sign is five-sided with a fluorescent yellow-green background and two school children pedestrian symbols in black — the standard design across Nova Scotia since 1 June 2001. When children are present, the maximum speed is 30 km/h where the approaching limit is 50 km/h, or 50 km/h where the approaching limit is higher.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The playground sign is a diamond showing a single running child.
A pedestrian crosswalk sign shows an adult figure above a striped crossing.
There is no separate daycare sign in the handbook.

question: Which shape and colour is reserved for the school area sign in Nova Scotia?
choices: Five-sided, with a fluorescent yellow-green background
Diamond-shaped, with a yellow background
Eight-sided, with a red background
Rectangular, with an orange background
explanation: The school zone sign is five-sided with a fluorescent yellow-green background and two school children pedestrian symbols in black. Its unusual shape and high-visibility colour are what make it recognisable at a distance.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Yellow diamonds are general warning signs.
The octagon is reserved for stop signs only.
Orange marks temporary conditions in work zones.

question: What does this sign indicate?
choices: The location of a school crosswalk
A school bus stop
The boundary of a school property
A playground entrance
explanation: This sign indicates the location of a school crosswalk. At school crossings, both drivers and pedestrians must obey the instructions of the crossing guard.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: School bus stops are not marked with this sign.
The sign marks a crossing point, not a property line.
Playgrounds have their own diamond sign.

question: Which of these signs tells you that reduced school-area speed limits may apply?
choices: A five-sided sign with a fluorescent yellow-green background and two black figures of children walking.
A fluorescent yellow-green diamond with the black silhouette of a running child.
A tall white rectangular sign with a black figure of a pedestrian walking toward the roadway centre above a baseline.
A green rectangular sign with a white bicycle symbol and route information.
explanation: Only the five-sided fluorescent yellow-green sign marks a school area. The others warn you to watch for particular road users but do not set a school-area speed limit.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The running-child diamond warns of a playground: reduce speed and watch for children.
The walking figure above a striped crossing marks a pedestrian crosswalk.
The bicycle symbol tells you to share the road with cyclists.

question: What does this sign mark?
choices: The location of a pedestrian crosswalk
A sidewalk that crosses the road
A pedestrian-only street
A bus stop
explanation: This sign indicates the location of a pedestrian crosswalk. Remember that every intersection has a crosswalk whether or not it is marked or signed — the sign draws attention to a particular crossing point.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The sign marks the crossing on the roadway, not a sidewalk.
It does not exclude vehicles from the street.
Bus stops are marked separately.

question: You are approaching this sign on a residential street. What action does it call for?
choices: Reduce speed and watch for children
Stop and check for children before proceeding
Sound your horn to warn children
Nothing in particular — it is an information sign
explanation: The playground sign means you are approaching a playground: reduce speed and watch for children. Children playing near the street may run out in front of you without warning, so anticipate it.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A stop is not required; a reduction in speed and heightened attention are.
Sounding the horn could draw a child toward the road.
The sign requires a change in how you drive.

question: You see this sign on a road into Halifax. What does it ask of you?
choices: Expect cyclists and share the road — they have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists
Cyclists must ride single file here
Motor vehicles are prohibited on this road
Cyclists must use the sidewalk on this section
explanation: This sign tells you to expect cyclists on the roadway. Under the Motor Vehicle Act, cyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists, and you must respect a cyclist's right to share the road.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The sign is addressed to drivers about the presence of cyclists.
The road remains open to motor vehicles.
Bicycles are road vehicles, not sidewalk traffic.

question: What does this sign mark?
choices: A railway crossing, at the crossing itself
A road closure ahead
An intersection ahead
A hazard in the middle of the road
explanation: Railway crossings are marked with a crossbuck sign, which has a white background with a red reflective border, used at the crossing itself. As you approach the tracks, look both ways and listen — trains can approach a crossing at any time.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Closures are signed with orange work-zone signs and barricades.
An intersection ahead is a yellow diamond warning sign.
Road hazards are marked with hazard markers or keep-right signs.

question: A small plate showing the numeral 2 is mounted below a railway crossbuck. What does it tell you?
choices: There are two sets of tracks to cross
Two trains use this crossing each day
The crossing is two metres wide
The speed limit is 20 km/h
explanation: A smaller sign below the crossbuck indicates if there is more than one set of tracks. This matters because after one train has passed you must check that another is not approaching on the second track before you move off.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The plate counts tracks, not train movements.
It is not a dimension.
It is not a speed limit.

subtopic: flashing red lights at a crossing
question: Flashing red lights are operating at a railway crossing with a crossbuck. What must you do?
choices: Stop, just as you would for any flashing red traffic signal, and only proceed when it is safe
Slow down and cross if you cannot see a train
Cross quickly before the gates come down
Sound your horn and proceed
explanation: When flashing red lights are used with crossbuck signs at a railway crossing, you must stop just as you would for any flashing red traffic signal, and only proceed when it is safe to do so. If the warning signal activates, you must stop before the gates lower across your side of the road, and you must not move through a crossing when the gates are lowered.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A train may be hidden by a curve, buildings or trees, and trains are quieter and faster than people expect.
Racing the gates is how vehicles get trapped on the tracks.
The horn does nothing to make the crossing safe.

question: Which vehicles should you expect to stop at every railway crossing, even when no train is coming?
choices: School buses, vehicles carrying passengers for hire, and vehicles transporting explosives or hazardous materials
Only school buses
All commercial vehicles
Only vehicles displaying a slow-moving-vehicle sign
explanation: Be prepared to stop for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses, motor vehicles carrying passengers for hire, or vehicles transporting explosives or hazardous materials — these are marked with placard signs. Leaving a safe following distance behind them prevents a rear-end collision at the crossing.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The requirement extends beyond school buses.
Not every commercial vehicle is required to stop.
The slow-moving-vehicle sign indicates a vehicle that cannot exceed 40 km/h; it is unrelated to this rule.

question: A train has just passed the crossing in front of you. What should you do?
choices: Wait and check that another train is not approaching before moving off
Move off immediately, since the crossing is now clear
Move off as soon as the gates begin to rise
Follow the vehicle in front without checking
explanation: Do not move immediately after the train has passed. First check to make sure that there isn't another train approaching — a second train can be hidden by the one that has just gone by, particularly where a plate below the crossbuck shows more than one set of tracks.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A second train on another track may be arriving from either direction.
The gates rising is not by itself confirmation that a second track is clear.
Following blindly means you are relying on another driver's check rather than your own.

question: Traffic is heavy and backed up beyond a railway crossing. What should you do before you move forward onto the tracks?
choices: Make sure the traffic ahead will not leave you stopped on the tracks
Move up as far as possible to keep the queue tight
Cross and stop on the far side of the tracks
Wait for the crossing lights to activate before deciding
explanation: Crossing gates will not trap you, but stopped traffic might. Be sure the traffic ahead of you will not stop you on the tracks before you move forward. Only enter the crossing when there is room for your whole vehicle on the far side.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Closing the gap is exactly what leaves vehicles stranded on the tracks.
Stopping partway across leaves part of your vehicle in the path of a train.
By the time the lights activate, a train is already approaching.

question: You see this yellow sign some distance before you reach any tracks. What is it telling you?
choices: You have reached the crossing and must stop at this sign
A train is occupying the crossing further ahead
A railway crossing is ahead — look and listen as you approach
The road ahead runs alongside a railway line
explanation: This is the advance warning sign for a railway crossing. It tells you a crossing is coming up, so look both ways and listen as you approach, because you may have to stop. The angle of the symbol on the sign reflects the angle at which the tracks cross the road. The crossing itself is marked by the crossbuck.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The crossbuck marks the crossing itself; this sign is posted in advance of it.
The sign is permanent and says nothing about whether a train is present.
It warns of tracks crossing the road, not running beside it.
